entities.text: High Court Of Delhi At New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2.  The appellant was convicted vide judgment dated 28.05.2015 for offence u/s 376/511 IPC and vide order on sentence dated 30.05.2015 was awarded sentence to undergo RI of 5 years with a fine of Rs 25,000/- for offence u/s 376/511 IPC and in default for fine further imprisonment of 3 months.
He was also awarded RI for a period of 15 years with a fine of Rs 50,000/- and further imprisonment for a period of 6 months in default of payment of fine for offence u/s 376 IPC.
Both sentences were directed to run after the expiration of the other.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant has already This is a digitally signed order.

4.
Learned APP has opposed the application on the ground that the appellant has been convicted for sentence offences and if released from Jail, he may not attend the proceedings of the appeal.
5. It is a settled proposition that in the cases of sentences, for a fixed term the appellate Court is required to consider the plea for suspension of sentence liberally.

Recently, the Supreme Court in Harish vs State(Nct Of Delhi) on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146914610/
1 Bherulal v. The State of Madhya Pradesh in SLP (Crl.) No.8388/2024 inter-alia held that suspension of sentence can be denied only when there are exceptional circumstances emerging from the record of the case to be declined such relief.

entities.text: Bherulal v. The State of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. Recently, the Supreme Court in Vishubhai Ganpatbhai Patel & ANR.
vs. State of GujaratCriminal Appeal no. 3415/2023 inter alia held and directed that grant of suspension of sentence may be favourably considered if there were no antecedents and more than 40% of the sentence has been undergone.
7. The perusal of the nominal roll indicates that as of 14.10.2022, the appellant has undergone a total period of around 9 years 4 months.

entities.text:
Vishubhai Ganpatbhai Patel & ANR.
vs. State of GujaratCriminal Appeal no. 3415/2023
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, as of now the total period of custody of the appellant is of around 11 years.
His conduct is stated to be satisfactory.
8. Be that as it may be, the appellant has already served around half of the sentence imposed.

Given the facts and circumstances of the case, the duration of incarceration, and considering that the appeal hearing may take some time, the appellant's sentence is hereby suspended during the pendency of this appeal on the appellant furnishing a personal bond in
